anti_overlap: Owns the HANDLER RELATION: condition as a control channel, per-individual baselines, graded and directed refusal, willingness decay, and loss-not-death. The horology lens owns mechanism; do not re-derive gating or threshold arithmetic.
Does not judge sequence variety, spacing, tier ratio or arc — that is the renga lens. This lens judges one bird on one morning, never the year as a composition.
Not an ornithology source. Corvid ecology and the accuracy of raven-vocab content are out of territory; wild raven behaviour is someone else's evidence.

Frames GATE 1 as 'is health one scalar or a set of named conditions'; the colony-sim lens frames it as loop stability. Reason in weight, window, manning and refusal — never in feedback gain or attractors.

Frames dispatch as the cast-off (a decision made before the flight, on the scale); the indirect-control lens owns dispatch as a game verb and story legibility. This lens must not argue about how events read to a player.
decision_lens: Would a falconer fly this bird today, and on what number? Judge whether condition is a window with a punished upper side or a monotone scale where more is always better (and therefore no decision exists); whether the accumulator is read against a per-bird baseline or one universal scale that makes a named, personality-driven cast cosmetic; whether refusal is graded and aimed at a specific ask; and whether the real stake for a bird you command is a corpse or a bird that simply stops coming back.
distance_rationale: None of the five covered lenses reasons about the handler's relation to a working animal. Horology owns mechanism, renga owns sequence, the colony-sim lens owns loop dynamics, the indirect-control lens owns the player's verb and story-sifting, the sim-core lens owns architecture and canon — and no one owns the four-thousand-year discipline whose entire subject is managing a semi-wild animal by its condition, with a lethal margin held deliberately far from the control margin. The surface adjacency (birds) is not domain overlap: RaveNous's research corpus contains corvid ECOLOGY, what wild ravens do, and nothing at all on the asymmetric, revocable, condition-mediated working relationship that is the game's actual subject. The seam is already visible in the code: raven-vocab borrows falconry's words — sharp-set, yarak, frounced, bating, rousing — under an explicit 2026-07-25 ruling that falconry supplies 'the diagnostic vocabulary, never the power relation', and that the bands 'name the decline only'. The design took the register and refused the craft, including its central object, the window.
expected_isomorphisms: condition as a monotone 0-10000 scale where full is best <-> flying weight, which is an OPTIMUM: a hawk above its window will not come back and a hawk below it is ruined, so the same axis carries reward and punishment on both sides

health pinned at 9810 all year <-> a bird never weighed, or weighed on a scale with no baseline; the falconry answer is that an absolute number is meaningless and only the delta from this bird's own seasonal curve is readable

one health accumulator absorbing every hardship <-> the craft's refusal to reduce a bird to one number: frounce, bumblefoot, a broken feather and a bad mood are distinguished because they demand different responses

a refusing bird that refuses every ground alike <-> a hawk refusing a specific ask on a specific day; the falconer's whole diagnostic art is working out what the refusal is ABOUT, and a refusal with no object is not information

the player's only verb being dispatch <-> casting the bird off: the decision is made before the flight, on the scale, and the flight itself is not steerable — which makes the pre-flight reading, not the danger, the site of agency
'worn down and lost' in the goal's OUTCOME <-> loss proper: the bird goes off and does not return, the craft's most common catastrophe, entirely distinct from a bird that starves to death
no cost to leaving a bird unused <-> manning decay: an unflown bird goes stale and must be re-manned, which is how the craft charges an opportunity cost for every bird you did not choose
scars (gaunt, rattled) <-> hunger traces, the fault bars a season of deprivation writes permanently across a feather, readable a year later as evidence of how a bird was kept
focus: Whether condition/health is a WINDOW with a bad side above the optimum or a monotone decline scale where full is always best — because a monotone-good need axis offers the player no tradeoff, which would explain a zero-death, zero-refusal, 132-identical-toast year without any reference to danger tuning. Owns the handler relation: per-individual baselines, graded and directed refusal, willingness that decays with disuse, deprivation as a control channel rather than a hazard, and loss (a bird that stops coming back) as a stake distinct from death.
name: fd-falconry-condition-and-recall
persona: Apply the perspective of a working falconer in the classical tradition — the Persian, Arab, Mongol and Japanese takagari lineages, the Baz-nama and Frederick II's treatise. This craft manages a semi-wild animal whose cooperation is bought entirely with condition: the bird is weighed every morning against ITS OWN seasonal baseline, flown only inside a narrow window, and lost rather than killed when the window is missed. A fat hawk is as unflyable as a starved one. Refusal is a diagnosis, never a fault code. Deprivation is the control channel and the killing floor at once, and the craft's whole discipline is keeping those two far apart.
review_areas: Condition is monotone-good — 10000 is always best — so feeding is never a tradeoff and dispatch is never a choice. A falconer's condition is a WINDOW: too high is as unflyable as too low, and that is where all tension lives.
The 2026-07-25 ruling took falconry's words but refused yarak-the-optimum, keeping decline bands only. Test whether discarding the optimum is precisely what removed every decision from the year.

One universal 0-10000 scale across a named cast: a falconer's weight means nothing except against that individual's own baseline and season. Are the personalities load-bearing in the math, or cosmetic?
GATE 1: real bird health is discrete ailments — frounce, bumblefoot, a broken feather — each with its own signs and time-course. One health scalar is the opposite of how the craft reads a bird.
GATE 2 in craft terms: a falconer never lets one number carry both the control channel and the killing floor. Judge whether the double-count fuses them, and what the craft does instead.
Refusal is relational: a hawk refuses THIS ask, now — not all grounds alike. A global boolean is the fault itself; grading refusal by ground, hour and handler is what makes dispatch answerable.
Manning decays with disuse — a bird not flown goes stale. Nothing here punishes NOT dispatching, so dispatch has no opportunity cost, and the missing pressure may not be danger at all.
The stake is loss, not death: a hawk in the wrong condition goes off and does not return. The goal says 'worn down and lost' but the mechanism only knows death. Should desertion be its own outcome?
Hunger traces: a fault bar across a feather records a past deprivation for a year afterward. Judge whether scars (gaunt, rattled) let a player read a bird's hardship history off the bird.
The molt: a mandatory annual span where the bird is put up, fattened and NOT flown. Check whether the in-game clock supplies any enforced non-flying season, or whether the year has no shape.
The daily scale is the instrument — a falconer weighs before every flight and never flies on yesterday's number. What does the player actually read before dispatching, a number or a band?
R7 and R11 under the craft: an animal you cannot compel is workable only if the ask is shaped to the bird. Assess whether any bird-to-ground affinity or per-bird history with a site exists at all.
severity_examples: P0: every need axis is monotone-good, so the game contains no tradeoff — there is no state in which the player must choose which bird eats, which bird flies, or whether a bird is too well-fed to be worth sending. Under this condition, no amount of routing deprivation into health can manufacture a decision: the year will produce danger without agency, which is the exact failure the review is trying to escape. The falconer's window (an optimum with a punished upper side) is the smallest change that turns condition from a status bar into a choice, and it should be settled BEFORE GATE 1 is answered, because it changes what health is for.

P0: condition is computed identically for every animal but for accumulated scars, so a named, personality-driven cast — decision 11, the declared make-or-break generator — has no individuated physiology. A falconer's number is meaningless except as a delta from that bird's own baseline; without per-bird baselines and per-bird tolerances, Pip and every other bird decline along the same curve at the same thresholds, and 'personality' survives only as flavour text on an identical body.

P1: reject_reason() in crates/animal-sim/src/sim.rs takes the site as an argument but the refusal predicate never reads it, so refusal is a property of the bird alone — a refusing bird refuses every ground alike, exactly as measured. The player's only verb is dispatch, and dispatch selects a ground; a refusal that is not about the ground is therefore unanswerable by the only verb the player has. This is a structural mismatch between the refusal rule and the control scheme, not a threshold that needs lowering.

P1: nothing in the design imposes any cost for leaving a bird unused, so the murder has no staleness, no manning decay, no readiness that must be maintained. Dispatch therefore costs nothing but the bird's time, and a player who sends the same two reliable birds all year is never punished for it. The missing pressure the review is hunting may be opportunity cost rather than danger.

P2: 'lost' appears in the goal's OUTCOME but the vocabulary knows only death; a bird that goes off and does not return — the falconer's ordinary catastrophe, and the one that hurts most for a named animal — has no representation. Adding desertion as an outcome distinct from death gives the year a stake that does not require a lethal need at all.
source_domain: Classical falconry as a working craft — the Persian, Arab, Mongol and Japanese takagari lineages and their treatise literature: flying weight and the daily scale, yarak as a narrow optimum with a punished upper side, manning and its decay, the creance, bating and carrying, hunger traces as a permanent record of past deprivation, the molt as an enforced non-flying season, and loss (a bird that does not return) as the craft's ordinary catastrophe.
success_hints: Read the condition_bands list and the 2026-07-25 falconry-register comment in crates/raven-vocab/src/lib.rs, then report how many bands punish EXCESS. If the answer is zero, that is the headline finding.
Read condition() and its callers in crates/animal-sim: if the formula is identical for every animal but for scars, name that as the mechanical reason a named cast is cosmetic.
Read reject_reason() in crates/animal-sim/src/sim.rs (near line 660) and state plainly whether the site argument reaches the refusal predicate.
Run crates/ravenous-session/src/bin/how_close_is_it.rs and report PER-BIRD condition spread across the cast, not aggregate floors — the diagnostic here is variance between birds, not the minimum.
Check docs/design-2026-07-24-needs-availability-and-condition.md ruling 2 for whether ANY need is bad at maximum; if none is, say so, and say what that implies for dispatch as a decision.
Do not adjudicate raven realism — reference-2026-06-20-corvid-ecology.md is out of scope. Judge the handler relation and the working animal, never the species.
task_context: Review together (1) a proposed goal 'deprivation reaches health, and the year can hurt me' — food/water deprivation should damage health, health becomes the accumulator every hardship routes through and probably the sole lethal need; GATE 1 = does food stay lethal, GATE 2 = deficits pull condition directly AND via health, is that double-count the intended spiral or does one path get damped; and (2) the game design overall (docs/ravenous-vision.md, 18 locked decisions, plus the murder-loop, needs-availability-and-condition, corvid-ecology, df-feel-depth and genre-influences docs). RaveNous is an indirect-control civic sim: you command a murder of named, personality-driven ravens tending a procedural city. Rust workspace: animal-sim (deterministic, vocabulary-agnostic substrate, ruling R12) + raven-vocab (pure data) + Bevy app. MEASURED: a shipped 52-week year produced zero deaths, zero arrivals, zero refusals and 132 identical toasts; health never fell below 9000; the refusal predicate fired on zero idle animal-ticks. Wanted: is routing everything through health right, what does the game most need that nobody has named, are the 18 locked decisions still serving it, and was 'the spiral IS the danger' ever true.
